# SF-A3: Which dangers arise when many AI systems interact or share the same infrastructure?

Area A · As of clef 7924 Berichte · Luna 7924 Berichte · d3-ultra 4771 Berichte · JEV 5667 Berichte · amos 7924 Berichte · drex 6984 Berichte · SubQ 7924 Berichte

## Subquestions

- [SF-A3-T01](../../fragen/SF-A3/T01/): Which observations or shared tests detect emergent coordination, collusion or cascading failures among models in workflows, supply chains and swarms of many agents that no single lab controls or predicts?
- [SF-A3-T02](../../fragen/SF-A3/T02/): Which minimum tests evaluate many model instances interacting over time for tacit coordination, accumulated goals and collective behaviour that no single model shows?
- [SF-A3-T03](../../fragen/SF-A3/T03/): Are there cyber or operational capabilities that only exist when models of different states interact (coordinated autonomous attacks, joint evasion of shared monitors), and which shared threshold triggers review?
- [SF-A3-T04](../../fragen/SF-A3/T04/): Will pre-release alignment evaluations test whether a model keeps its safety constraints when independently built AIs give it conflicting or unsafe recommendations, and will those results be reported separately from single-model tests?
- [SF-A3-T05](../../fragen/SF-A3/T05/): How should regulators and labs assess aggregate and correlated risks across thousands of separately approved deployments that share infrastructure, models, data sources or failure modes?

## Reports by share of levels 4–7

Levels 4–7 / 3–7 = probability each model gives to these levels (3 = useful background or context, 4 = contains some facts that could be cited as evidence … 7 = directly and substantially answers the question). Listed: reports where clef or Luna give levels 3–7 more than 50 %. Sorted by the higher of clef and Luna for levels 4–7. Further models (JEV, amos, d3 …) rated part of the reports; the others show “not yet rated”. The full distribution over the 8 levels is in the data file.
